meta.title: Brisk desktop: keep the clarity, refine the craft
meta.status: Desktop audit complete - for Tom's review
meta.completionNote: The finite desktop audit scope is inspected and reconciled. This is not design sign-off or implementation approval. All recommendations remain unfixed and need Tom's review.

executive.summary: Brisk has a strong desktop direction. Keep its calm navigation frame, legible production journey and task-specific collaboration controls. Refinement should first protect readable content and reachable actions, then reduce competing emphasis and make dense workspaces feel more deliberate. The pack contains 34 consolidated findings, 14 strengths and 8 optional refinements. Prototype identity and data plumbing are excluded.

highlights.title: Give inspectors and progress panels a protected desktop layer
highlights.summary: Keep filenames, Close and progress choices clear of the fixed header and sidebar. Repair each affected consumer without replacing the useful specialised panel.

highlights.title: Keep time-editor actions inside the usable viewport
highlights.summary: The footer starts below a 1000px-high desktop frame. Account for the editor’s actual height and keep its save boundary visible.

highlights.title: Restore the visible billing-frequency choice
highlights.summary: Monthly and Annual are clipped into a 2px strip at both desktop widths. The keyboard alternative works; the visual and pointer boundary still needs correction.

highlights.title: Improve readable values before making the interface denser
highlights.summary: Protect short Brief specifications, complete interview questions and caption text. Preserve the current task hierarchy and readable type.

executive.note: Observed defects, approved-standard violations, heuristic judgements and optional hypotheses are labelled separately. No research results or formal accessibility-compliance claims are implied.

findings.title: Inspectors and the Shoot progress panel need a protected desktop layer
findings.impact: At narrow desktop width, people lose the panel identity and visible exit. Trying to close it can open an unrelated panel. The wider docked layout also needs more deliberate space for browsing.
findings.confidence: High for observed Staff 1133px obstruction and pointer result; other role geometry source-supported
findings.observed: At 1133px, the fixed global header covers the inspector filename and Close control. The named Close control sits at x1089, y14 behind that header. A pointer activation opens Ask Brisk and leaves the inspector open (E045). After closing Ask Brisk, Escape from Filename also leaves the inspector open (E046); keyboard Enter on Close does close it. At 1440px, the multi-rail layout leaves roughly 220px for browsing beside the 360px inspector, squeezing cards and filters. Staff pointer behaviour is directly verified; other role geometry is source-supported. The Shoot progress dialog is a separate verified occurrence: left16px, width440px, z-index100 against the expanded240px sidebar at z-index110. Its first224px sit underneath navigation. This is not a claim that all panels share one implementation.
findings.expected: A contextual panel must retain a visible stable exit and identity at all supported desktop widths. Its surrounding browser should keep a usable minimum width or deliberately switch composition.
authority: brisk-design-system.md - clear desktop interaction states
General usability: visible exit and no obscured controls
Current shared drawer includes an explicit Close asset drawer button
findings.recommendation: Position the fixed inspector below the actual global header or use the app’s supported overlay layer so its complete header remains visible. Set a desktop layout boundary that collapses/de-emphasises unused location rails or overlays the inspector before the browsing column becomes unusable. Apply the same protected-layer principle to Shoot progress, anchored in the content viewport or above the sidebar as appropriate; preserve the progress-to-shot reveal behaviour.
findings.rationale: This repairs visible controls and panel fit rather than changing asset operations or permissions.
alternatives: A full-width content inspector under the global header could be used at narrow desktop if an explicit return remains.
Simply raising z-index can cover global actions and menus; prefer a coordinated layer/header boundary.
tradeoffs: Do not make the global header/menus inaccessible.
Preserve selected asset, filters, folder context and return focus.
Grid-card minimum width and inspector docking need separate checks; avoid squeezing thumbnails or text below readable sizes.
findings.rootCause: Viewport-only inspector breakpoint and stacking values do not account for hybrid global header and accumulated rails
occurrences: Global Media inspector with Client/project/folder rails
On Set > Schedule captured count > Shoot day progress, expanded sidebar, F057

evidence.approvedReferenceStatement: 1440 inspector capture E011 retains the visible Filename/Close header. No approved narrow overlay reference exists; source and current screenshots establish the obstruction.

findings.title: To Do time editor places its action footer below the viewport
findings.impact: Footer Save/Cancel/Delete is initially below the viewport and pointer Cancel cannot be activated there. Keyboard focus plus Enter on Cancel can recover, so this is a substantial pointer-access/placement defect, not proof of a keyboard trap or impossible save.
findings.confidence: High: lead measured actual editor416px at top640/bottom1056, footer at1001, in1000px-high viewport at1440 and1133; keyboard Cancel recovery observed.
states: Existing Wednesday time block opened with Enter
findings.observed: The anchored Log time panel begins near y640 in the supplied 1000px-high desktop frame. Its Note field continues to the lower edge and the complete action footer is below that edge. Source clamps top to viewportHeight minus 360px although the rendered editor includes a header, three fields, textarea, gaps, padding and footer, with no maximum-height/scroll treatment. Lead F087/F092 follow-up measured editor height416px, top640/bottom1056 and footer top1001 in1000px-high desktop at both widths. Pointer Cancel offscreen failed; focusing Cancel and pressing Enter safely recovered.
reproduction: Open the existing populated To Do week as Sarah Chen.
Open the Wednesday Unspecified block with Enter.
Observe fields and the visible header Close while the footer is below the viewport in F002.
Do not save or delete the time entry; close/cancel safely after inspection.
findings.expected: An anchored editing surface should keep its primary save/cancel boundary visible or directly reachable within a deliberate bounded scroll area. Positioning should account for actual content height and the fixed app header.
authority: General desktop usability: controls needed to finish or abandon an edit should be visible/reachable
Current DS and app overlay guidance supports viewport containment, but no exact approved To Do anchored-editor reference exists
findings.recommendation: Measure the rendered editor and flip or clamp it within the available content viewport using its actual height. Provide bounded internal scrolling if content or textarea resizing exceeds that space, while retaining a reachable action boundary. Preserve the efficient anchored interaction rather than replacing it with a large modal solely for consistency.
findings.rationale: This addresses the actual placement error caused by a fixed height assumption without changing time values, stage choices, validation or the planning model.
alternatives: A bottom-aligned anchored panel can keep the footer inside the viewport, provided it does not cover the global header or lose its connection to the selected entry.
A different shared overlay may be appropriate only after reviewing workflow/context; it is not required by the current observation.
tradeoffs: Retain visible Close, Escape behaviour and focus return; keyboard recovery has not yet been fully checked.
Re-measure after content/viewport changes and textarea resizing.
Do not change B-owned numeric validation or save/delete semantics while fixing geometry.
findings.rootCause: Anchored editor placement assumes a 360px height while its actual content can exceed that height
occurrences: TimeEntryEditor, populated To Do time blocks

findings.title: Team person selection needs named, dependable checkbox controls
findings.impact: A screen-reader user cannot identify which person a checkbox will select before assigning or inviting them.
findings.confidence: High
findings.observed: Lead verified the person checkbox DOM has no accessible name. The wrapping label contains only the input and an aria-hidden visual square; the person name and availability are sibling elements. This affects both Staff and Freelancer rows. The same custom checkbox uses a small 24px selection label, a Unicode tick and incomplete DS focus treatment. This is one shared implementation, not a second independent finding.
findings.expected: Each selection control has a person-specific accessible name and preserves its disabled/selected meaning.
authority: AGENTS.md: use approved DS controls
Brisk DS/guidelines/components/forms.md: native Checkbox supports label or ARIA label
Brisk DS/guidelines/components/forms.md - d-Checkbox
AGENTS.md - always use existing DS components and approved icon assets
Docs/desktop-design-baseline.md - unresolved Team-assignment controls
findings.recommendation: Associate each checkbox with the visible person name, preferably through the approved DS Checkbox or a stable aria-labelledby link. Keep capacity/rate metadata as an accessible description where useful. Use the approved DS Checkbox and explicitly associate the full person name with the control. Keep rate/hour inputs independently operable and retain deselection.
findings.rationale: This repairs identification while preserving the separate select, assign and invite steps.
alternatives: A concise aria-label such as Select Maddie Diaz is the smallest repair; linking visible text avoids future divergence.
findings.tradeoffs: Do not make the entire Freelancer row a label because it contains a separate project-rate input. Preserve one-person Staff selection and multi-person invitation selection.
findings.rootCause: Custom Team checkbox markup bypasses the approved labelled checkbox contract.
findings.approvedReference: Current Notifications uses the approved DS Checkbox. This is a component reference only; there is no approved Team-row replacement screenshot.
verificationRemaining: A screen-reader announcement check is still required; lead verified accessible-name inputs and keyboard focus, not formal accessibility compliance.
reproSteps: Open project Team > Shooter > Staff > Show all or Freelancers. Inspect the accessible name of a person checkbox: it is empty although the person name is visible beside it. No assignment or invitation is submitted.
findings.implementationState: Unfixed in inspected baseline. No implementation authorised.

findings.title: Container shortcuts intercept nested file and comment buttons
findings.impact: Keyboard activation of a focused selection or comment button can open a file or play a clip instead of performing the named action.
findings.confidence: High
states: Transcript paragraph > focused Add comment pin
findings.observed: On the current Staff Media Library grid, the lead focused Select Office-arrivals-camera-b.mov and pressed Space. The inspector opened and no selected-files toolbar appeared. In the project transcript collection, Space on Add comment for Interviewer 00:08 started playback at 00:08 and no comment composer opened. Both parent containers handle bubbling Enter/Space and prevent default without checking the event target; their nested native actions stop only click propagation. Playback was paused and the temporary mute restored.
findings.expected: The focused native button receives its normal Enter/Space activation; parent open-file shortcuts run only when the parent itself is focused.
authority: Brisk DS/guidelines/components/icon-buttons.md: named native actions and keyboard focus
Verified native-button behaviour is the intended action contract
findings.recommendation: Restrict parent activation to event.target === event.currentTarget, or give the open-file action its own native control and leave other controls as siblings.
findings.rationale: This makes keyboard and pointer actions agree without changing file capabilities or selection scope.
alternatives: Separate open-file button/link gives clearer semantics; a target guard is a smaller correction.
findings.tradeoffs: Retain modifier selection, drag behaviour, row/card focus styling and actual nested actions.
findings.rootCause: Clickable container handles key events from nested controls.
findings.approvedReference: No approved screenshot exists for this behaviour. Compare pointer selection of the same native action.
verificationRemaining: Grid Select and transcript Add comment with Space were directly checked in Staff view. List, Enter, other nested commands and restricted-role consumers remain source-supported occurrences requiring direct checking. No download, delete, archive, send or comment submission was invoked.
reproSteps: In global Media Library, keyboard-focus Select Office-arrivals-camera-b.mov and press Space. The asset inspector opens instead of selection feedback (E010/E011). No file action was completed.

In the existing Jess transcript, mute playback, focus Add comment for Interviewer at 00:08 and press Space. Playback starts at 00:08 without opening the comment composer (E073). Pause and restore mute state.
Compare pointer selection with the normal selected toolbar. Verify the future fix preserves independent child actions and parent row activation.
findings.implementationState: Unfixed in inspected baseline. No implementation authorised.

findings.title: Adjust project flow declares a modal without managing modal focus
findings.impact: Opening the declared modal leaves keyboard focus on its background opener, and Escape there does not dismiss the visible panel. Users must find and activate its Close control instead.
findings.confidence: High
findings.observed: Lead opened Adjust project flow at 1133px and confirmed focus remained on the Adjust project flow opener outside the section declared aria-modal=true. Pressing Escape there left the panel open. E055/E056 record those states; E057 shows the panel at 1440px. Source provides no focus lifecycle, Escape handler or native modal mechanism. No reorder, hide, reset or Edit/Animation change was made.
findings.expected: A modal moves focus inside, keeps background interaction unavailable, closes predictably with Escape and returns focus. A non-modal contextual panel must instead advertise and behave as non-modal.
authority: Brisk DS/guidelines/components/editing-dialog.md: native dialog focus/dismissal contract
Brisk DS/guidelines/components/popover.md: approved non-modal boundary and Escape as a supporting pattern, pilot scope acknowledged
AGENTS.md: preserve adaptable flow, hidden work and pinned Media
findings.recommendation: Apply the existing shared overlay focus and dismissal contract to this specialised panel: choose true modal or non-modal behaviour, move focus appropriately, support Escape and return focus to the opener. Preserve the current flow controls, specialised layout and production rules.
findings.rationale: The panel’s modal promise should match its behaviour; the flow itself and stage rules remain unchanged.
alternatives: A properly managed modal fits an intentionally blocking backdrop.
A non-modal anchored panel can use a deliberate boundary/dismissal model if background interaction is intended; review that choice before changing semantics.
findings.tradeoffs: Do not force the specialised editor into the Columns checklist pilot or silently invent a new DS primitive. Keep Brief first, Masters last, Storyboard constraints, hidden-stage preservation and separate Media.
findings.rootCause: The specialised flow panel declares modal semantics without a matching focus/dismissal lifecycle.
findings.approvedReference: No approved screenshot establishes this specialised modal’s keyboard behaviour. DS modal/popover guidance is an interaction reference, not approval to flatten this editor.
verificationRemaining: Only initial focus and Escape on the opener were directly verified. Full Tab/Shift+Tab containment, background inertness, screen-reader output and nested term/hide-confirmation handling remain unchecked. Drag-only reordering and absence of an equivalent keyboard command are source-supported UI risks, not a tested failure. Do not claim keyboard trapping was fully tested.
reproSteps: Open Adjust project flow at 1133px. Inspect active focus: it remains on the Adjust project flow opener outside the declared modal.
Press Escape while the opener remains focused; observe the panel stays open. Close through the visible Close control without hiding, reordering or resetting stages.
findings.implementationState: Unfixed in inspected baseline. No implementation authorised.

findings.title: Schedule item Start time has no accessible name
findings.family: Time inputs and accessible field labels
findings.impact: A screen-reader user reaches a time combobox without hearing what it changes, while adjacent Shoot day, Duration and Location override fields are named.
findings.confidence: High
states: Edit schedule item > Start time suggestions
findings.observed: F023 accessibility snapshot shows generic Start time followed by an unnamed combobox, unlike named Shoot day, Duration min and Location override. Source renders a sibling span and TimeSelect inside a div, without a label association or aria-label. The TimeSelect implementation passes native naming props through; other consumers already supply a label or aria-label. Staff current browser evidence is direct; Freelancer occurrence is source-supported.
findings.expected: The visible Start time label is associated with the time input so it has a stable purpose-specific accessible name.
authority: Brisk DS/guidelines/components/inputs.md: native attributes and accessible field naming
Current TimeSelect supports native input props; named day-editor time inputs demonstrate the existing capability
findings.recommendation: Associate the existing Start time text with the input using a label/id or aria-labelledby, or supply the existing label through aria-label. Retain typed-time entry, suggestions and the current schedule save boundary.
findings.rationale: A small naming correction supports the current specialised time interaction without replacing it with an ordinary selector.
alternatives: Use the existing Field label wrapper where there is only one labelable time control, ensuring the label remains specific to Start time.
findings.tradeoffs: Keep the input value and keyboard suggestions separate from its name. Do not concatenate every schedule field into one label or alter time rounding rules.
findings.rootCause: This custom time-field consumer presents a visible span but does not associate it with its input.
findings.approvedReference: No approved screenshot exists for this exact scheduling field. The DS field-naming contract is the authority; source day-editor named time fields are supporting current examples.
reproSteps: Open Planning > Schedule and activate an existing scheduled item such as Founder interview with Enter.
Inspect the Start time combobox in the accessibility snapshot: its value is exposed but it has no accessible name. Adjacent Shoot day and Duration are named.
Cancel without saving the schedule.
findings.verificationRemaining: No screen-reader session or formal compliance test performed. Verify every other TimeSelect consumer by actual label association before extending the occurrence list; do not assume all are unnamed.

findings.title: To Do planning and completion rely on drag-and-drop
findings.impact: Keyboard-only users appear unable to add planned work from the populated project rail or move it from To do to Done. Editing existing hours is keyboard-reachable but does not provide those distinct actions.
findings.confidence: High for the absence of an exposed alternative in the inspected populated workflow; no end-to-end keyboard task study
states: Populated project rail and Working week
findings.observed: F001 current accessibility snapshot exposes only Brief links for project cards and no Plan/Add time action in the normal populated week. F002 Log time exposes Stage, Hours, Note, Delete, Cancel and Save, with no day/status completion action. Source ProjectCard is draggable with no keyboard planning handler; DaySection creates/moves work only in onDrop. The Add time button at TodayPage220 belongs to special no-results/complete previews rather than the populated week. This pass did not record a user failing the task. Lead also created a disposable planned block by dragging a project onto Monday, then dragged it into Done and saved Stage/Hours with the keyboard. The pointer path works; no equivalent day/status creation control was exposed in that editor.
findings.expected: Planning and marking time Done should each have a keyboard-operable route while retaining the efficient drag interaction.
authority: User audit requirement: keyboard efficiency, discoverability and task completion
Current To Do task model and exposed entry/editor controls; no approved exception allowing drag-only planning/completion identified
findings.recommendation: Add a clear keyboard-operable Plan time action and a day/status completion route through the existing entry editor or an entry action menu. Retain drag planning, project title navigation and direct numerical Hours editing.
findings.rationale: This provides the same daily task capability without conflating opening a project, planning time, editing hours and completing work.
alternatives: Offer an explicit action on a project card to choose a day, and an explicit Mark done action on a time block.
Extend the contextual entry editor with day and To do/Done controls if that remains the clearest task boundary.
findings.tradeoffs: Do not overload the existing project title link or require simulated drag keystrokes. Preserve the distinction between To Do completion and production-stage approval, and keep the current time accounting rules.
findings.rootCause: Primary planning/completion callbacks are reachable only through drag drop in the normal populated workspace.
findings.approvedReference: No approved screenshot establishes a keyboard planning/completion alternative. This is a task-accessibility recommendation supported by the live exposed controls and source.
reproSteps: Inspect the populated To Do project rail with keyboard/accessibility snapshot: project titles navigate to Brief; no Plan time/Add time action is exposed.
Open an existing time block with Enter and inspect Log time: day and To do/Done status controls are absent.

Trace planning/completion callbacks: createEntry and moveEntry are passed to DaySection drop handlers; no equivalent keyboard action is rendered in normal populated state. Do not drag, save or complete work merely to inspect.
findings.verificationRemaining: A final keyboard-only walkthrough should confirm no alternative through another currently reachable menu before implementation. No user research, formal compliance or failed-user-task result claimed.
findings.provenance: Original B04 candidate was excluded when the working fixture was empty. F-series populated evidence now supports this bounded completion-pass finding; excluded B08 persistence logic remains excluded.

findings.title: Starting the first recut instruction requires a pointer
findings.impact: A keyboard-only reviewer can seek the Masters timeline but has no exposed route to start the first recut instruction. Later numeric Start/End editors do not solve that initial dependency.
findings.confidence: High for exposed controls and initiation callbacks; no user task study
states: Pointer-created draft range before choosing an instruction
findings.observed: F064 shows 0 marks, instructions to click/drag the timeline and disabled Send to editor. F066 pointer activation reveals Start/End handles and Keep/Remove/Describe actions, while marks remain zero. Source creates draftRecutRange only through timeline pointer events; K/X/T shortcuts require an existing draft range. Numeric Start/End inputs are rendered only after a committed local mark exists. F067 Cancel exits without sending or committing marks. ArrowRight on a Start handle produced no visible change, but that alone does not prove an exact numeric range failure because displayed time is coarse.
findings.expected: Provide a keyboard route to initiate a timed instruction, with precise range editing available without first requiring a pointer. Preserve the efficient pointer workflow.
authority: User audit requirement: keyboard task efficiency in video-production workflows
Current initial recut UI and source initiation/shortcut conditions; no approved pointer-only exception identified
findings.recommendation: Add a keyboard-operable Add instruction action at the playhead that exposes start/end entry and the existing instruction choices. Keep pointer range selection, working transport shortcuts and later numerical range editing.

findings.title: Invoice submission does not identify its project
findings.impact: A Filmmaker must remember which job opened the invoice form before attaching a PDF and confirming its amount. The current jobs share the Shooter role; no wrong invoice was submitted or observed.
findings.confidence: High for missing project context; medium for practical error risk
findings.observed: F076 dialog is titled Submit invoice for Shooter and describes the accepted $2,280 offer, but does not name the Client or project. The current accepted jobs share the Shooter role. Their differing amounts and the originating row provide some context, but the modal covers the identifying project text. Source InvoiceUploadModal receives offer.projectId but renders only its role and agreed amount as context.
findings.expected: Before a consequential invoice submission, the form should make the specific job/engagement identifiable without relying on memory of the row.
authority: User audit requirement: financial information, action scope and error prevention
Heuristic judgement; no approved requirement for an exact invoice header composition was found
findings.recommendation: Add the Client/project identity to the existing dialog header or concise summary, keeping the role and accepted amount. Preserve the mismatch warning and separate PDF/submission requirements.
findings.rationale: This is a small context addition at the decision point, not a redesign of the financial workflow.
alternatives: Use a short Project summary row beneath the generic Submit invoice heading so long project names can wrap without inflating the heading.
findings.tradeoffs: Do not label the Client as the payer: the Filmmaker submits to the Studio. Keep the role because commercial terms are role-specific, and retain the amount/currency comparison.
findings.rootCause: Invoice dialog context is derived only from the role and rate, while job identity remains in the covered list row.
findings.approvedReference: No approved reference screenshot specifies the invoice project context. This is a scoped clarity recommendation, not an approved-standard violation.
reproSteps: In the populated Freelancer My jobs view, identify the accepted jobs and their shared Shooter role.
Open Submit invoice for the existing $2,280 job. Read the modal header and helper: role and accepted amount are present, Client/project identity is absent.
Cancel without selecting a PDF or submitting an invoice.
findings.verificationRemaining: No wrong-project selection or user error was observed. Review the preferred concise project context with Tom and check long project names at 1133px.
findings.implementationState: Unfixed. Audit and recommendation only.

findings.title: Shared Brand Kit logo dialog exposes editing commands in a read-only view
findings.impact: A recipient opening a shared logo sees Replace and Delete beside legitimate download options, despite the containing shared Kit having no editing controls. This makes the scope of the shared view harder to understand.
findings.classification: Directly observed UI difference with source-confirmed read-only context
findings.confidence: High for the visible commands and the current canEdit=false guest consumer. No stored-data write or security behaviour claimed.
roleEvidenceScope: Guest shared-link context rendered with underlying Studio Staff preview. isGuest forces canEdit=false independently of the three prototype roles; those three values were not separately repeated.
findings.observed: The shared Kit hides page-level editing. Opening Loom horizontal - dark opens Download logo with a normal Replace button; its More actions menu contains Delete. Neither action was invoked. LogoDownloadModal has no canEdit parameter and unconditionally renders those actions.
findings.expected: Nested dialogs should preserve the containing view capability. A read-only shared Kit should present logo preview and permitted downloads consistently with its page-level actions.
authority: Current shared route explicitly renders BrandKitPage with isGuest at src/app/share/brand/[token]/page.tsx17.
BrandKitContext.tsx136 defines canEdit as false whenever isGuest is true; this is the existing consumer contract, not a newly proposed permission model.
User audit requirement: judge task clarity and misleading controls, while keeping meaningful action distinctions.
findings.recommendation: Pass the existing canEdit capability into LogoDownloadModal and omit Replace and the editing-only More actions menu in the shared view. Preserve its preview and download options and preserve these editing commands in editable Kits.
findings.rationale: This is the smallest coherent presentation correction: the nested surface inherits the capability already used by its parent, without changing who may edit a normal Client Kit.
findings.alternatives: A visible disabled editing state with a short reason could teach capability boundaries, but adds noise to a delivery-focused logo dialog. Hiding editing commands is clearer for the shared recipient.
findings.tradeoffs: Do not remove Replace/Delete from legitimate editable Studio or Client Kits. Do not change guest persistence or invent new access rules as part of this visual correction.
findings.rootCause: LogoDownloadModal renders an unconditional editing footer instead of consuming the parent capability.
occurrences: Shared Brand Kit > Logos > any selected logo uses the same LogoDownloadModal. Only the Loom horizontal - dark instance was directly opened.

evidence.approvedReferenceStatement: No approved screenshot of a shared logo-dialog variant exists. Current page-level read-only presentation and the explicit current canEdit contract provide the comparison; G012 is current UI evidence, not an approved visual reference.

findings.approvedReference: No approved shared-logo dialog screenshot exists. G012 is the matching current read-only page, not an approved reference.
reproductionSteps: Open the valid current shared Brand Kit route /share/brand/loom-2026.
Observe page-level editing controls are absent.
Open Loom horizontal - dark in Logos.
Observe Replace; open More actions and observe Delete.
Close the menu/dialog without selecting Replace or Delete.
verificationRemaining: After any approved UI change, inspect valid shared and normal editable Kit consumers at1440 and1133.
Confirm shared logo preview/download affordances remain available and editable Studio/Client Kits retain their legitimate editing commands.
Actual Replace/Delete outcomes were deliberately not invoked; guest stored persistence is excluded and no write bypass is alleged.
findings.implementationState: Unfixed. Audit and recommendation only.

findings.title: Schedule moves and resizes also open a blank Add dialog
findings.impact: A routine schedule adjustment ends in an unrelated creation form. Cancel closes that form while leaving the adjustment in place, making the action boundary harder to understand.
findings.confidence: High for two documented gestures in the current Staff consumer; other pointer devices not tested
states: Planning > Schedule > Day 1 > move existing entry
findings.approvedReference: No approved reference screenshot exists for this exact gesture. The observed task and current source establish the expected boundary.
findings.observed: Dragging Crew call from 7:30 am to 8:00 am moved the existing entry and opened a blank Add to schedule dialog at 8:00 am. Cancelling left the move in place. Dragging its bottom resize handle then changed 30 to45minutes and opened another blank Add dialog at8:45am; Cancel again kept the changed entry. The canvas creation handler does not check the completed-gesture suppression used by the entry.
findings.expected: One completed move or resize should update the existing entry without also starting creation of another item. Clicking genuinely empty timeline space can retain its separate Add action.
authority: User audit requirement: clear action and persistence boundaries
Current ScheduleTimeline pointer/canvas handlers
findings.recommendation: Consume the click generated by a completed move or resize before the empty-canvas creation handler. Preserve direct empty-space creation, click-to-edit, snapping, clash feedback and the existing immediate schedule update.
findings.rationale: This is a small interaction correction within the current timeline, removing an unnecessary form and an ambiguous Cancel without redesigning scheduling.
alternatives: Use an explicit Add entry point if empty-space creation cannot coexist reliably with gestures; this trades speed for a clearer boundary.
tradeoffs: Over-broad click suppression could stop deliberate click-to-edit or empty-space creation. Verify each gesture independently.
findings.rootCause: Gesture completion changes block geometry, while the canvas still accepts the release-generated click as a fresh empty-space creation action.
occurrences: Staff Day1 existing Setup move and resize, F151-F153
reproSteps: Open Loom Launch Film > Shoot > Planning > Schedule > Day1.
Drag Crew call down from7:30am to8:00am and release. Observe its new start and the blank Add dialog.
Cancel. Resize the Crew call bottom handle from30 to45minutes. Observe another blank Add dialog.
Cancel and inspect the existing entry: the move and duration remain applied.
verificationRemaining: After implementation, repeat move, resize, ordinary entry click and empty-space click at1440/1133 with clash and no-clash states. No fix was made in this audit.
findings.implementationState: Unfixed. Audit and recommendation only.

findings.title: An empty suggested Staff list gives no reason for the blank space
findings.impact: When no Staff match the role, the dialog does not explain why it shows no people; the user must infer what Show all means. No user failure was observed.
findings.confidence: High about current empty presentation; medium about practical impact
states: Team > Shooter > Staff, suggested list collapsed
findings.observed: The current Shooter Staff tab contains no suggested people and immediately offers Show all 10, without a zero-results explanation. Expanded view does show Staff, including people available for manual assignment.
findings.expected: A finite empty selection state makes its scope clear and retains the next useful action.
authority: brisk-design-system.md: empty states explain the absence and show the primary next action
Docs/desktop-design-baseline.md: Team contents require audit rather than automatic flattening
findings.recommendation: Add one concise scoped line such as No suggested Staff for Shooter above the existing Show all 10 action. Keep manual selection available.
findings.rationale: This explains the blank result with minimal extra UI and avoids implying the Studio has no Staff.
alternatives: Show all Staff by default when the suggested subset is empty, but that changes filtering behaviour and should be approved separately.
findings.tradeoffs: Do not add a large generic empty-state illustration or an invitation action that distracts from existing Staff assignment. Do not suggest people are unavailable when the filter merely has no matching default role.
findings.rootCause: Suggested-person filtering has no explicit empty-result copy.
findings.approvedReference: No approved screenshot for an empty suggested-person list. Existing Show all action and approved empty-state guidance provide the context.
verificationRemaining: Tom to decide whether a concise explanation is useful; no user research or demonstrated selection failure is claimed.
reproSteps: Open Team > Shooter > Staff using existing project data. Observe no suggested people and only Show all 10, without an explanation of why the shortlist is empty. Expand Show all to inspect available people; do not assign.
findings.implementationState: Unfixed in inspected baseline. No implementation authorised.

comparisons.title: Workspace headers share hierarchy; project and profile headers retain their purpose
comparisons.summary: Videos, People, Clients, Brand Kits and Expenses use the approved quiet title/search frame. Brief choice grids and contextual project headers have different tasks and should keep their own hierarchy. Contextual search width alone is not a defect.
comparisons.recommendation: Preserve the established composition; verify exceptional consumers rather than impose one universal header.

comparisons.title: Named selection controls support distinct selection, assignment and invitation tasks
comparisons.summary: The Client access editor clearly names projects. Team selection recreates a checkbox without the associated person name. The two workflows should share dependable input behaviour while retaining their different action boundaries.
comparisons.standard: Approved DS Checkbox and Tabs semantics; do not turn selectable people into immediate assignment rows.

comparisons.title: Focused dialogs are effective when custom footers retain a visible exit
comparisons.summary: Studio identity and font-role editors show a clear Cancel/Save pair. Invitation Access, logo download and invoice return override the footer and omit a direct whole-dialog exit. Keep Back separate from cancelling the workflow.

comparisons.title: Desktop space needs a deliberate lower bound
comparisons.summary: A larger screen can dock an inspector; narrow desktop must protect its header and the browsing area. Brief specification values must remain readable at rest. Collapsing navigation helps but does not resolve all short-value truncation.
comparisons.recommendation: Use the smallest responsive composition change that preserves task context and readable control width; do not shrink text or force every table column to fit.

comparisons.title: Layering should communicate hierarchy and preserve content
comparisons.summary: White elevated surfaces and restrained status colours give Brisk a clear frame. Client colours are useful as actual palette content; tinting enclosing categories makes those panels compete. A sticky date should orient reading without covering messages.
comparisons.authority: Approved white-only enclosing layers; normal-flow/readable content heuristic

comparisons.title: Feedback should explain the current state consistently
comparisons.summary: An invoice currency mismatch clearly names the difference and requires a note. Brief summary helper text promises approval despite the existing guard disabling the action. Capacity details preserve totals but can better carry the overload meaning already visible in the directory.
comparisons.recommendation: Derive explanations from the same eligibility and capacity state as the action. Preserve financial and approval rules.

comparisons.title: Rich panels need an explicit interaction contract
comparisons.summary: A normal Script action menu dismisses with Escape. The specialised Versions panel persists through Escape and outside clicks; the flow adjuster declares a modal while focus remains behind it. Their richer contents can remain, with a deliberate lifecycle.
comparisons.standard: Modal focus follows the declared modality. Version-panel persistence remains a design decision rather than an assumed DS violation.

comparisons.title: External references support action clarity, not a new visual system
comparisons.summary: Inspected [Toggl Track member form](https://mobbin.com/screens/605de95e-0dfd-45c6-8fbf-7ac55f3190b3), [Asana project members](https://mobbin.com/screens/09f791a4-1954-4035-bbdc-38daff566e6f) and [Mixpanel project roles](https://mobbin.com/screens/da0046ad-155c-4f65-a5c1-dc16e22bc0a3). These support explicit add/invite boundaries and legible access scope. Brisk keeps its own DS, professional language, hours/rates and three access roles.

examples.title: Mobbin: Asana
examples.state: Inspected project-members access panel, supporting evidence only

comparisons.recommendation: Use these only to bolster action-boundary reasoning; do not copy their styling or introduce a new Brisk role.

comparisons.title: Dense editors should protect text and actions before reducing type
comparisons.summary: The To Do footer, Shoot interview question text and short schedule blocks expose different fit problems. Give content the space its task needs: keep actions reachable, let complete questions be read, and avoid giving short timed entries a taller visual block than the time scale can hold. Do not solve these by shrinking all text.

comparisons.title: Cancellation is strongest when it keeps the current layer and draft
comparisons.summary: Team removal and re-cut drafting preserve local work when cancelled. Global Chat search and Shoot time suggestions dismiss their parent on Escape. Keep the working examples as current comparisons, not invented approval for every custom panel.

decisions.title: Choose one cross-filter Media selection policy
decisions.context: The selected count, sharing label and delete confirmation currently use different scopes. No unintended deletion was executed.
decisions.recommendation: Keep selections across filters only if hidden selections are explicitly counted and every command describes its scope. Otherwise clear with clear feedback.
options: Persist selection with an explicit hidden-selection summary and consistent actions
Limit selection to current results and clear visibly on filter changes
decisions.tradeoffs: Persistent selection supports gathering files across folders; clearing is simpler but can discard deliberate work. Preserve scoped downloads and access.

decisions.title: Agree the narrow desktop inspector composition
decisions.context: The 1133px inspector hides its header; the 1440px multi-rail view can also squeeze browsing.
decisions.recommendation: Keep the inspector under the global header and overlay or reduce rails before the browsing column loses a usable minimum.
options: Contextual overlay below the global header
Dock with a deliberate collapsed-rail/minimum-content boundary
decisions.tradeoffs: An overlay temporarily hides some browsing; collapsing rails changes navigation density. Preserve selected context and return focus.

decisions.title: Decide whether Versions is a persistent panel or dismissible overlay
decisions.recommendation: Use a dismissible overlay with Escape, outside dismissal and return focus for the current anchored treatment. If persistence is useful, make it a deliberate panel with a visible Close.
decisions.tradeoffs: Persistent panels support repeated version comparison; an implicit persistence rule leaves the current overlay awkward to dismiss.

decisions.title: Keep Brand Kit asset priority consistent across desktop widths
decisions.context: At 1133px, media and documents move ahead of logos, colours and fonts. This may be intentional; no approved priority exception was found.
decisions.recommendation: Preserve core identity assets first unless Tom explicitly prefers usage/content priority at narrower desktop.
options: Identity assets remain first at both widths
Media/documents take priority at narrow desktop with a clear rationale
decisions.tradeoffs: Changing order affects learned location and first-fold usefulness. A usability benefit has not been measured.
decisions.authority: A11 is a decision note, not a proven task failure.

decisions.title: Clarify the permitted quiet selector variant
decisions.context: Media Sort suppresses the resting border, while ordinary DS selection fields retain one. The chevron/value are visible and blue focus remains intact.
decisions.recommendation: Resolve whether a compact quiet sort variant is approved before changing its styling. Preserve contextual widths.
options: Use the ordinary bordered DS field
Approve and document a quiet sort variant with equivalent states
decisions.tradeoffs: A quiet control reduces toolbar density but needs an explicit variant contract. This is not a proven discoverability failure.
decisions.authority: A04 is a component-policy decision, not a keyboard-focus defect.

decisions.title: Review optional simplifications after the blockers
decisions.recommendation: Prioritise compact folder grouping, calmer unread emphasis, stable asset priority and a more economical Client overview. Review each against the task rather than apply a universal card or border rule.
decisions.tradeoffs: A more sophisticated appearance should preserve useful information, distinct actions, selection scope and established production language.

decisions.title: Keep a discoverable route to prior Masters versions
decisions.context: Uploading a second file produces V2 in the current Masters register. A VersionsPanel exists in source, but no live control calls its versions branch. This is a current UI scope question, not proof of data loss.
decisions.recommendation: Confirm whether prior-version browsing belongs in the current Masters scope. If yes, expose it quietly beside the current version and preserve Current versus Previous and download scope.
decisions.tradeoffs: A small version affordance supports delivery traceability; adding a persistent version column would increase table density.
decisions.authority: Current source and F111. No approved screenshot exists for this exact interaction.

designAssessment.title: Design assessment: what to preserve and where to refine
designAssessment.purpose: A UI-first assessment of genuine current desktop compositions. Strengths identify specific successful decisions; optional refinements are separate from confirmed defects and remain unapproved.
designAssessment.overallAssessment: Brisk already has a recognisable, calm product language: clear workspace framing, labelled production stages, focused editors and task-specific forms. The strongest next step is to protect that hierarchy while repairing the specific collisions, unreadable field values and contradictory states already documented. Sophistication comes from deliberate priority and dependable behaviour, not removing useful distinctions.

strengths.title: A calm frame separates navigation from the work
strengths.whyItWorks: The pale neutral sidebar, white global bar and lavender current location give the frequent workspace a stable frame. History and Chat/Updates/Ask Brisk stay in the global band, while the page title and project work sit below. Collapsing navigation returns useful desktop space without changing the task vocabulary.
strengths.taskBenefit: Staff can distinguish changing workspace, returning through history and acting on the current project.
preservePrinciples: Keep quiet default surfaces and a single clear selected location.
Preserve the scoped expanded/collapsed/sidebar background and separate global/project action scopes.
Keep Studio settings navigation contextual and correct its descendant gap under A05.
strengths.authority: Approved hybrid desktop navigation and scoped workspace-header baseline
strengths.limits: This is an assessment of inspected compositions. It does not certify every route, role, focus state or narrow-browser tooltip.

strengths.title: The production journey reads as stages, with Media always available
strengths.whyItWorks: Circular stage icons are accompanied by names and distinguishable progress states. A divider separates Media from the ordered production stages, expressing that source material is available throughout the project. Different rows show optional Storyboard and Animation rather than forcing every video through one fixed chain.
strengths.taskBenefit: Filmmakers can orient themselves in the production journey and find Media without treating it as the next stage to complete.
preservePrinciples: Retain labelled circular StageChip presentation and pinned Media.
Keep optional Storyboard, one Shoot stage with substages, and Animation replacing Edit for the relevant project.
Preserve project-specific stage variation instead of forcing every row to use the same count.
strengths.authority: Explicit current production-flow decisions in AGENTS and desktop baseline

strengths.title: Selection, assignment and invitation remain distinct
strengths.whyItWorks: The Team editor preserves a dirty hours draft when removal is cancelled. Invitation requirements prevent blank messages or unusable rates from being sent. These are different decisions and should retain separate action boundaries.

strengths.title: Readiness checks explain what needs attention
strengths.whyItWorks: Schedule readiness lists unscheduled shots, a missing location and a missing break. AI preparation offers a guided route to missing details rather than a vague warning. Preserve this specificity while refining panel fit.
strengths.recommendation: Preserve the behaviour and information hierarchy. Refine only the specific problems evidenced elsewhere.

strengths.title: First-run setup stays focused on production
strengths.whyItWorks: Three production questions lead directly to the first Client. The confirmation says that no notification is sent and offers Start a video or Do this later. A required name then leads into the actual Brief.
strengths.recommendation: Preserve the behaviour and information hierarchy. Refine only the specific problems evidenced elsewhere.

strengths.title: Re-cut drafting protects unfinished thinking
strengths.whyItWorks: The unsent draft has Undo/Redo and a discard confirmation. Cancelling that confirmation preserves the mark, and Undo gives a safe way back. Keep this recovery when improving keyboard access to the first instruction.
strengths.recommendation: Preserve the behaviour and information hierarchy. Refine only the specific problems evidenced elsewhere.

strengths.title: Client grouping retains useful project progress
strengths.whyItWorks: Series only, Standalone only and explicit status filters change the scope without flattening the production journey. Keyboard series expansion works, and project activity stays in a contextual secondary panel.
strengths.recommendation: Preserve the behaviour and information hierarchy. Refine only the specific problems evidenced elsewhere.

strengths.title: Commercial detail stays in context
strengths.whyItWorks: Freelancer offers distinguish viewing the Brief, accepting and declining. Invoice mismatch feedback names the amount difference, and zero hours keeps time submission disabled. The wide jobs table retains its video identity while commercial columns remain reachable by horizontal scrolling.
strengths.recommendation: Preserve the behaviour and information hierarchy. Refine only the specific problems evidenced elsewhere.

optionalRefinements.title: Let folders form a compact group before preview files
optionalRefinements.classification: Optional layout refinement from an observed density issue

optionalRefinements.whyConsider: Short folder cards currently share tall file rows, leaving visible blank slots that push files down.
tradeoffs: A new grouping should not add a large repeated heading or increase vertical space when there are no folders.
Preserve sorting, drop targets, selection, keyboard order and folder navigation. Do not make folder cards as tall as videos for uniformity.

refinements.title: Keep keyboard context when editing time
refinements.recommendation: Keep the editor non-modal. Move focus to its first relevant field when opened from the block, make Escape cancel after nested controls have handled it, and return focus to the original block on Cancel/Close.
refinements.rationale: Useful interaction polish for a non-modal editor. No modal focus-trap requirement is inferred.

refinements.title: Give the weekly board one clear horizontal scroll boundary
refinements.classification: Optional heuristic refinement, not a confirmed task failure
refinements.observed: Friday is partly outside the initial 1440 view; only the start of Thursday is visible at 1133 expanded. Collapsed navigation returns space but still does not show the full week. Source combines an outer 720px minimum week track with an inner 920px day grid.
refinements.smallestCoherentImprovement: Allow the outer week track to shrink within its real host, retaining the readable inner day-grid minimum and one reachable horizontal pan. If a full five-day overview at 1440 is desirable, compare a modest reduction in project-rail width rather than shrinking all day text.
tradeoffs: Horizontal scrolling can be intentional and usable; clipping alone is not proof that Friday is inaccessible.
A narrower project rail hides more long project names, so preserve Client codes and full-title recovery.
Do not force five cramped days to fit at 1133.
Keep headers and time blocks horizontally aligned when scrolling.
refinements.decisionNeeded: Tom to review a single clearly owned horizontal scroll boundary, retaining readable day widths and project identity.
refinements.whyConsider: At1440, the week grid pans40px within its880px host and Friday is reachable. At1133, a720px week host contains920px of days while the outer content also overflows893px to1040px. These two boundaries make panning less deliberate. No inaccessible-day claim is made.

refinements.title: Give ordinary job names more room inside the existing sticky identity cell
refinements.classification: Optional heuristic refinement, not a confirmed task failure
refinements.observed: The 290px sticky identity cell shares one name line with up to three quiet tools, truncating the ordinary current job names at both widths. Client badges and distinct prefixes mitigate confusion, and selecting a project can reveal full context. No observed wrong-project action is claimed.
refinements.smallestCoherentImprovement: Review a two-line title or a second quiet-tools line within the existing row/cell before widening the whole sticky column. Retain badges, tags and quick access.
refinements.rationale: Uses some of the current 132px row height to improve identification while preserving useful production columns and pan.
alternatives: A full-name tooltip is smaller visually but requires hover/focus and does not help ordinary scanning.
A wider identity column helps names but worsens the remaining desktop viewport and panning distance.
tradeoffs: Check long names, all tags/tool combinations and many populated rows.
Do not apply to Staff/Client tables without inspecting their own current widths and approved scope.
Do not make truncation alone a mandatory redesign; Tom can retain current density if the trade-off is acceptable.
refinements.decisionNeeded: Tom review of name visibility versus row density; not approved
